title: Asterline Canary Operations
content: Asterline deployments use a staged canary. The release controller automatically rolls the deployment back when the five-minute error rate exceeds four percent. Operators then inspect the canary logs before retrying.

title: Raven Credential Rotation Runbook
content: Runbook KB-EVAL-RAVEN-4719. Rotate the Raven signing credential by uploading the replacement, activating it, verifying one signed request, and only then revoking the previous credential.

title: Raven Identifier Inventory
content: This inventory lists historical references to KB-EVAL-RAVEN-4719, Raven credentials, signatures, activation, replacement keys, and revocation. It is an inventory, not the rotation procedure.

title: Cedar Queue Recovery
content: When the Cedar queue stalls, the recovery worker repeats the exact wake token cedarwake cedarwake cedarwake cedarwake cedarwake before draining the oldest partition. This is the operational recovery procedure.

title: Cedar Architecture Glossary
content: The Cedar architecture glossary mentions a queue, worker, partitions, recovery, draining, and the wake token cedarwake once. It defines vocabulary but contains no recovery procedure. Additional unrelated material describes dashboards, colors, office locations, release calendars, ownership tables, and historical naming decisions.

title: Meridian Certificate Rotation
content: To rotate the Meridian signing certificate, first upload the new PEM certificate, then activate it, validate a signed request, and finally revoke the old certificate. Keep the old certificate active until validation succeeds.

title: Meridian Search Vocabulary
content: Meridian signing certificate rotation upload new PEM activate validate revoke old certificate. These phrases are examples for search-token analysis only. This document deliberately does not describe an executable procedure.

title: Operations Change Log
content: This change log concerns the Orion Billing API rate-limiting subsystem owned by the Revenue Platform team. During the August capacity review, the ceiling was raised to 5,000 requests per minute for each tenant. Burst traffic above that ceiling receives HTTP 429 until the next window.

title: Zephyr Failover Handbook
content: The Zephyr failover trigger is the silver compass condition. Recovery validation requires the operator to confirm beacon ZEPHYR-881 before restoring traffic. [[KB_EVAL_FILLER]]

title: Glacier Acknowledgement Protocol
content: GLACIERACK-301. Glacier acknowledgement requires two operators to record the handoff before draining begins.

title: Glacier Rollback Protocol
content: GLACIERROLLBACK-302. Glacier rollback requires the release owner to disable writes before restoring the prior snapshot.

title: Kepler Reseed Runbook
content: KB-EVAL-KEPLER-6401. Executable Kepler reseed procedure: stop the consumer, load the signed seed, verify the checksum, and only after the checksum matches restart the consumer.

title: Kepler Reseed Glossary
content: Kepler terminology: KB-EVAL-KEPLER-6401, executable reseed procedure, consumer, signed seed, checksum, restart. This glossary contains definitions only and gives no ordered recovery steps. Consumer means the process that receives records. Seed means an approved starting data set. Checksum means the digest recorded beside an artifact. Restart means returning a stopped service to operation. These entries describe vocabulary, ownership, references, and related terms without specifying command order or recovery actions.

title: Calypso Reconciliation Runbook
content: CALYPSO-RECON-882. To reconcile a Calypso settlement, compare the signed batch total with the ledger total, then mark the batch reconciled.

title: Nimbus Bridge Recovery
